# Kernel footprint: mass.f90 (prototype P1)

**Base:** FireX, branch `AMReX`, commit `36975d765f` (36975d765fcead401e14b094a04f910ac42eab8a, 2026-09-24), path `Source`. All file:line citations below refer to this tree.
**Table:** `kernel_footprint_mass.csv` (337 rows), generated by `tools/inventory/kernel_footprint.py mass`.
**Scope (P1):** a per-box POINT_TO_MESH shim that runs the **unmodified** mass.f90 kernels on a static two-level AMReX hierarchy.

## 0. How the table was built, and how far to trust it

- **Resolution.** Every identifier in the executable statements of the target routines is resolved with host/USE awareness (same resolver as the other inventory tables). Each is classified as one of:
  - `mesh_ptr`: a MESH_POINTERS pointer, i.e. a MESH_TYPE component of the mesh chosen by POINT_TO_MESH;
  - `mesh_direct`: `MESHES(NM)%…`;
  - `nested`: a component of a WALL / BOUNDARY_COORD / … local pointer;
  - `module_global`;
  - `dummy`;
  - `local_alias`: a local pointer, with its `=>` targets listed. Attribution is flow-insensitive, so every target is listed.
- **Access classes.** `write` means the base of an assignment target. `read`. `arg` means an actual argument of a CALL; the callee is in the `callees` column. `ptr_target` means the right-hand side of `=>`. `inquiry:ALLOCATED` and similar.
- **Extent.** Each subscript is evaluated symbolically against the enclosing DO bounds, using IBP1 = IBAR+1 (same for J and K).
  - `wall:<expr>` marks subscripts driven by wall-cell coordinates (BC%II, IIG, …). These lie in 0..IBP1: II is the ghost/solid cell and IIG the gas cell.
  - `whole` marks a whole-array reference, which touches the full allocation including all ghost layers.
  - `idx:<v>` marks a scalar subscript.
- **Checks.** All 1,159 line citations in the CSV were checked automatically: each cited line contains the entity name, with 0 misses. The ghost-width claims below were then confirmed by reading the source.
- **Rows and routines covered.**
  - mass.f90, the core rows: MASS_FINITE_DIFFERENCES (mass.f90:20-357), DENSITY (mass.f90:365-991), and DENSITY's internal routines CHECK_MASS_DENSITY (mass.f90:775-963) and CLIP_PASSIVE_SCALARS (mass.f90:966-989).
  - Callees outside mass.f90 in the per-step path:
    - GET_SCALAR_FACE_VALUE and its internal MP5 (func.f90:1330-1487);
    - GET_MOLECULAR_WEIGHT (func.f90:1700-1707) and GET_SPECIFIC_GAS_CONSTANT (func.f90:1714-1721);
    - CURRENT_TIME (func.f90:23);
    - POINT_TO_MESH (mesh.f90:505-916).
  - Optional callees, off in a plain P1 case: SETTLING_VELOCITY (soot.f90:25-177; only runs for depositing species with gravitational or thermophoretic settling, mass.f90:411, 612) and SET_EXIMADVFLX_3D (ccib.f90:8002-8042; CC_IBM only, mass.f90:460, 648).
  - Not traced: ROTATED_CUBE_RHS_ZZ (ccib.f90:6396) and VD2D_MMS_Z_SRC (turb.f90:3491). Both are verification-test only (PERIODIC_TEST = 7/21/22/23).

## 1. Per-step call context (main.f90, time loop main.f90:695-1213)

| step | call | ghost/boundary inputs produced before it |
|---|---|---|
| predictor | `MASS_FINITE_DIFFERENCES(NM)` main.f90:767 | Uses RHO, ZZ and U/V/W from the previous corrector. Their ghosts come from `MESH_EXCHANGE(4)` (main.f90:959) and then `WALL_BC` (main.f90:1009), which calls `ASSIGN_GHOST_VALUE` (wall.f90:54, 282-388). U at interpolated faces comes from `MATCH_VELOCITY` (main.f90:1120). |
| predictor | `DENSITY(T,DT,NM)` main.f90:780, inside CHANGE_TIME_STEP_LOOP, so it may run more than once per step; FIRST_PASS guard at mass.f90:408 | The FX/FY/FZ just computed, UVW_SAVE, DEL_RHO_D_DEL_Z (divg.f90:411), and D_PBAR_DT (divg.f90:1519). |
| after predictor | `MESH_EXCHANGE(1)` main.f90:790, then `WALL_BC` main.f90:838 | These fill the RHOS/ZZS ghosts that the corrector MASS_FINITE_DIFFERENCES needs. |
| corrector | `MASS_FINITE_DIFFERENCES(NM)` main.f90:948 and `DENSITY` main.f90:949 | US/VS/WS from VELOCITY_PREDICTOR (main.f90:863), `MESH_EXCHANGE(3)` (main.f90:909), and `MATCH_VELOCITY` (main.f90:914), which also writes UVW_SAVE (velo.f90:2732-2774). |
| after corrector | `MESH_EXCHANGE(4)` main.f90:959 | — |

**Exchange depth.** MESH_EXCHANGE codes 1 and 4 pack **two cells deep** (II1 and II2 = II1∓1) of RHO(S) and ZZ(S), plus MU, KRES, D and Q (pack main.f90:3301-3345, unpack main.f90:3704-3733). ASSIGN_GHOST_VALUE then writes the first ghost `BC%II` and the second ghost `BC%II2` (wall.f90:342-386; BC%II2 is set at init.f90:3340-3347). The second ghost gets neighbour data only when the tangential face areas match, |AREA_RATIO−1|<0.01, and neither the second interior cell nor the neighbour's second cell is solid (wall.f90:351-377). At every level jump it is a zero-gradient copy of the first ghost (wall.f90:382-386). A shim that wants bit-parity at a coarse/fine interface must reproduce this copy, not a true second-layer interpolation.

**Net ghost requirement for P1 (cell-centred RHO(S) and ZZ(S)): 2 layers**, face-adjacent only. This holds for the default limiter SUPERBEE (cons.f90:710) and also for MINMOD, CHARM (DNS default, read.f90:1862) and MP5 (U(I+IM1)…U(I+IP2), func.f90:1375-1480). CENTRAL and GODUNOV need only 1 layer (func.f90:1351, 1361-1364). The padded product loops (mass.f90:70-76, 201-209) touch edge and corner ghosts too. The one-layer items are: CELL_INDEX, CELL, DX/DY/DZ, and PRESSURE_ZONE (in SETTLING_VELOCITY only).

## 4. WALL / CELL / obstruction dependencies

1. **Wall-cell loops.**
   - MASS_FINITE_DIFFERENCES loops over **all** wall cells IW = 1..N_EXTERNAL_WALL_CELLS+N_INTERNAL_WALL_CELLS (mass.f90:93-188 and 224-320). It uses WALL(IW)%BOUNDARY_TYPE, %BC_INDEX and %B1_INDEX; BOUNDARY_COORD%II,JJ,KK,IIG,JJG,KKG,IOR; and BOUNDARY_PROP1%RHO_F and %ZZ_F(1:N_TRACKED_SPECIES).
   - What it does with them:
     - thin-obstruction zero flux (mass.f90:108-117);
     - boundary face flux = RHO_F·ZZ_F for every non-INTERPOLATED boundary (mass.f90:119-128);
     - off-wall flux re-computation (mass.f90:133-186).
   - At INTERPOLATED_BOUNDARY faces (mesh or box interfaces), the boundary flux is **not** overwritten. It is the limiter value computed from the 2 ghost layers.
2. **External-wall loops in DENSITY.** These loop over IW = 1..N_EXTERNAL_WALL_CELLS only (mass.f90:424-436, 595-608).
   - They replace the face velocity at interpolated faces with UVW_SAVE(IW).
   - The corrector uses EXTERNAL_WALL(IW)%BOUNDARY_TYPE_PREVIOUS (mass.f90:598), which is set in MATCH_VELOCITY (velo.f90:2667; ccib.f90:5409).
   - This relies on the invariant that **external wall cells occupy IW = 1..N_EXTERNAL_WALL_CELLS and share their index with EXTERNAL_WALL and UVW_SAVE**.
3. **CELL_INDEX / CELL.** The kernels use CELL(CELL_INDEX(I,J,K))%SOLID to skip solid cells in every interior loop (mass.f90:446, 508, 530, 559, 573, 623, 690, 712, 741, 755, 811, 885, 950, 983), and SOLID/EXTERIOR of the ghost cell (mass.f90:108, 239).
4. **WALL_INDEX as a mass-redistribution barrier.** CHECK_MASS_DENSITY moves clipped mass only to neighbours whose face has `WALL_INDEX(±n)==0` (mass.f90:831-836, 907-912). Every mesh-boundary face of a gas cell has a wall cell (init.f90:3298 sets CELL(ICG)%WALL_INDEX(−IOR)=IW for external walls too), so no mass is pushed into ghost cells. DELTA_RHO values written at 0/IBP1 stay at 0, and only 1:IBAR is applied (mass.f90:854, 934).
   - Consequence for the shim: **every box face, whether a same-level box/box face or a coarse/fine face, must look like an external wall cell** with WALL_INDEX set. Otherwise CHECK_MASS_DENSITY would redistribute mass into ghost cells and lose it.
5. **Off-wall correction.** This reads CELL(CELL_INDEX(II±1,…))%WALL_INDEX(±IOR) and indexes II+2 / II−2 (mass.f90:140-182). It assumes at least 2 owned cells normal to every wall, i.e. box size ≥ 2 in each direction.
6. **No direct OBSTRUCTION access.** Obstructions enter only through CELL%SOLID, CELL%EXTERIOR, CELL%WALL_INDEX and internal wall cells (IW > N_EXTERNAL_WALL_CELLS).

## 5. Cross-mesh access

- **Direct access: none.** mass.f90 never references OMESH, MESHES(NOM), NOM or EXTERNAL_WALL%NOM/IIO_*. The only MESHES reference is the mesh itself: `ALLOCATED(MESHES(NM)%M_DOT_PPP)` (mass.f90:477, 639). GET_SCALAR_FACE_VALUE, GET_MOLECULAR_WEIGHT and GET_SPECIFIC_GAS_CONSTANT do not touch mesh data except through arguments. SETTLING_VELOCITY is also free of cross-mesh access. SET_EXIMADVFLX_3D reads only `MESHES(NM)%CC_NREGFACE_Z` (ccib.f90:8022).
- **Indirect dependencies.** All cross-mesh coupling arrives through state prepared by other routines:
  - ghost RHO(S)/ZZ(S), 2 layers deep: MESH_EXCHANGE(1/4) plus ASSIGN_GHOST_VALUE, including the area-weighted coarse/fine average (wall.f90:319-339);
  - the boundary-face velocities U(0)/U(IBAR) (MATCH_VELOCITY averaging, velo.f90:2724-2803) and UVW_SAVE;
  - B1%RHO_F/ZZ_F (WALL_BC, e.g. wall.f90:854, 866);
  - zone-global PBAR/D_PBAR_DT.

## 6. Uniform-grid and single-level assumptions

1. **Limiter formulas are undivided.** The TVD ratio R = ΔU_up/ΔU_loc (func.f90:1375-1385, 1396-1406, 1417-1431) and the MP5 coefficients (func.f90:1460-1485) assume locally uniform spacing across the 4-5 point stencil. FDS already applies them unchanged on stretched grids. On an AMReX level every box is uniform, so this holds as long as the ghost cells are filled **at the box's own resolution**.
2. **Ghost cell spacing = own spacing.** DX(0)=DX(1) and DX(IBP1)=DX(IBAR) (read.f90:1306-1307). CHECK_MASS_DENSITY uses DX(I±1), DY(J±1) and DZ(K±1) as neighbour volumes (mass.f90:801-828, 875-904). For a coarse/fine face these are the own-level sizes, not the neighbour's. That is irrelevant as long as WALL_INDEX blocks redistribution across the face (§4.4).
3. **The flux divergence is metric-correct.** mass.f90:447-450 and 624-627 use per-cell RDX, RDY, RDZ, R and RRN, so stretched grids are fine. No XS/XF/global coordinates are used, except XC/ZC in the MMS test.
4. **Coarse/fine flux mismatch (structural, not a code bug).** Each side computes its own boundary-face flux: FX(0) from its own ghosts, times its own U(0), which DENSITY restores to UVW_SAVE, the pre-average value (mass.f90:424-436, 595-608).
   - No reflux step exists, so the coarse-face flux ≠ Σ fine-face fluxes.
   - The same holds between equal-resolution FDS meshes (each uses its own U(0)).
   - For P1, the mismatch is quantifiable by comparing FX·U·area on both sides.
5. **Owned extent = 1:IBAR** in every loop. Faces run 0:IBAR. Allocations are hard-wired to −1:IBP1+1, 0:IBP1, etc. (init.f90:524-541, 586-620, 670-705).

## 7. What the shim must provide per box for mass.f90 to run unchanged

1. **A MESH_TYPE instance per box**, selected via `POINT_TO_MESH(NM)` (mass.f90:42, 397). NM is a box id; there is no hard-coded mesh 1 in mass.f90. It needs:
   - IBAR/JBAR/KBAR = box size and IBP1… = size+1;
   - box size ≥ 2 in every direction (§4.5).
2. **Cell-centred arrays with FDS bounds**:
   - RHO, RHOS, TMP, ZZ, ZZS and WORK_PAD with `-1:IBP1+1`;
   - RSUM, D_SOURCE, M_DOT_PPP (optional), DEL_RHO_D_DEL_Z, SWORK4, WORK4, WORK5, PRESSURE_ZONE and CELL_INDEX with `0:IBP1`.
   - The kernels depend on these exact lower bounds (pointer remaps at mass.f90:81-83 and 212-214 preserve LBOUND). A MultiFab with ngrow=2 maps to −1:IBP1+1 only if the Fortran view is created with the matching lower bound.
3. **Face arrays**:
   - U/V/W, US/VS/WS and WORK_U/V/W with `-1:IBP1` in the normal direction and `0:xBP1` in the tangential directions;
   - FX/FY/FZ with `0:IBP1 ×3` and species `N_LOWER_SCALARS:N_TOTAL_SCALARS` (index 0 is used when FLUX_LIMITER_MW_CORRECTION);
   - ADV_F* only if STORE_SPECIES_FLUX.
   - Boundary faces 0 and IBAR must hold the FDS-convention values: the MATCH_VELOCITY average for the flux, with UVW_SAVE = the pre-average own value.
4. **Ghost fill before each MASS_FINITE_DIFFERENCES call.** RHO(S) and ZZ(S) need **2 face-adjacent layers**, filled at the box's own resolution:
   - same level: copy;
   - coarse/fine: the FDS rule (fine side: injection from the one coarse cell, ARO=1; coarse side: area-weighted average of the covering fine cells, wall.f90:319-339).
   - Edge and corner ghosts need finite values only.
5. **1-D grid metrics**: DX, DY, DZ, RDX, RDY, RDZ, RRN and XC/ZC on `0:IBP1` (with DX(0)=DX(1) and DX(IBP1)=DX(IBAR)), and R on `0:IBAR`.
6. **Wall-cell structures for every box face.** Box faces are EXTERNAL_WALL entries IW = 1..N_EXTERNAL_WALL_CELLS, numbered first. Each carries:
   - WALL%BOUNDARY_TYPE (INTERPOLATED_BOUNDARY for box/box and coarse/fine faces), BC_INDEX and B1_INDEX;
   - BOUNDARY_COORD II/JJ/KK (ghost cell), IIG/JJG/KKG (gas cell), IOR, and II2… (second ghost);
   - BOUNDARY_PROP1 RHO_F/ZZ_F (used only for non-interpolated boundaries);
   - EXTERNAL_WALL%BOUNDARY_TYPE_PREVIOUS;
   - UVW_SAVE(IW).
   - Internal wall cells (obstructions) follow at IW > N_EXTERNAL_WALL_CELLS.
7. **CELL array**: CELL(IC)%SOLID, %EXTERIOR and %WALL_INDEX(−3:3), with WALL_INDEX nonzero on every box-boundary face of a gas cell (the CHECK_MASS_DENSITY barrier, §4.4). CELL_INDEX must cover 0:IBP1.
8. **Zone state copies**: PBAR, PBAR_S (0:KBP1, 0:N_ZONE), D_PBAR_DT and D_PBAR_DT_S (0:N_ZONE), identical on all boxes.
9. **Per-box scalars**: CLIP_RHOMIN/MAX and DT_RESTRICT_COUNT.
10. **Upstream inputs** (produced outside mass.f90): DEL_RHO_D_DEL_Z (DIVERGENCE_PART_1, divg.f90:411), M_DOT_PPP/D_SOURCE (if allocated), UVW_SAVE and BOUNDARY_TYPE_PREVIOUS (MATCH_VELOCITY), B1%RHO_F/ZZ_F (WALL_BC). For a mass-only P1 these can be frozen or prescribed: set M_DOT_PPP unallocated, DEL_RHO_D_DEL_Z=0, and UVW_SAVE = U at interpolated faces.
11. **Globals**: PREDICTOR, SOLID_PHASE_ONLY=F, ICYC>1 (otherwise DENSITY returns early, mass.f90:390), FIRST_PASS, PERIODIC_TEST=0, CC_IBM=F, the species tables, RHOMIN/RHOMAX, N_ZONE, I_FLUX_LIMITER. Serialize T_USED(3) or accept a race.
